title: 2**53 + 1 is a different number in Python than it is once it becomes a float
assumption: Adding 1 to a very large whole number (like an invoice ID or a total expressed in minor units) always produces a distinguishable result.

input.display: 2**53 + 1 as a Python int vs as a JS Number/float
input.description: An invoice total or running ledger balance expressed in cents that has grown past 9,007,199,254,740,992 (Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) - implausible for a single invoice, plausible for a cumulative all-time platform total - and then passed through a float or JSON.parse in JavaScript.

what_goes_wrong: In Python, `2**53 + 1 == 2**53` is False - they're exact, distinct integers. The moment either is converted to (or ever existed only as) an IEEE-754 double, `float(2**53 + 1) == float(2**53)` is True: both round to the identical double, because doubles only have 53 bits of mantissa and the gap between representable values at that magnitude is already 2.
why: A double has a 52-bit stored mantissa (53 bits of precision with the implicit leading bit), so it can represent every integer exactly only up to 2**53; above that, the spacing between representable doubles grows (it's 2 between 2**53 and 2**54, then 4, and so on), so 2**53 + 1 has no exact double representation and rounds to the nearest representable value, 2**53 itself. Python's native `int` is arbitrary precision and unaffected, which is exactly why this only bites once a number crosses into a float - via JSON, via JavaScript's single Number type, via a database driver that returns a float, etc.
affects: any IEEE-754 double used to hold an integer id or count

repros.code:
a = 2**53
b = 2**53 + 1
print(a == b)
print(float(a) == float(b))

fix: Never put an invoice ID, account balance, or any value that might exceed 2**53 (~9 quadrillion) through JavaScript's Number type or through JSON if the source has more precision - use a string for the ID/balance in JSON and parse it with a BigInt or arbitrary-precision type on the receiving end.

test_cases.note: their_function(x) that stores or compares large integer ids/totals must still tell 9007199254740992 and 9007199254740993 apart afterward; routing them through a float/JS Number makes them identical.
